recent_posts.title: Making AI Write Android Code Our Way: A Practical Guide to Agent Skills
recent_posts.summary: Medium's small Android team shares how they use Cursor's AGENTS.md and custom 'skills' (Markdown runbooks stored in .agents/skills/) to make AI coding assistants generate code that matches their team's conventions. They built 13 skills across four categories: scaffolding (new screens, modules, use cases), migration (Material 2→3, ViewModel patterns), pattern enforcement (feature flags, analytics, referrer tracking), and workflow automation (deeplinks, translations, unit tests). Key lessons: skills are living documents that improve iteratively, hyper-specificity beats generality, and consistency across a small team is the primary win. They also describe how agents can write new skills by analyzing existing PRs, and outline future plans for scoped rules and automated release diff commands.

recent_posts.title: Medium seeks principal backend engineer for platform evolution
recent_posts.summary: Medium is hiring a Principal Backend Engineer to lead the evolution of their core backend systems that power reading, writing, and discovery for millions of users. The role involves partnering with leadership to define engineering strategy, modernizing the codebase, setting technical standards, and mentoring engineers across teams. This is a fully remote, hands-on leadership position focused on building scalable, reliable systems while maintaining Medium's mission of elevating human voices and authentic content.

recent_posts.title: Migrating to Apollo Kotlin 4 on Medium Android App
recent_posts.summary: Medium's Android team migrated from Apollo Kotlin 3 to 4, encountering significant cache-related challenges. The migration exposed issues with their programmatic cache ID implementation, leading to frequent CacheMissException errors. They resolved this by switching to declarative cache IDs, adding __typename to all operations, and implementing custom exception handling for different fetch policies. The team also created extension functions for cache updates and added custom type adapters for scalar values, ultimately improving cache hit rates and overall GraphQL implementation robustness.

recent_posts.title: Learnings from optimising 22 of our most expensive Snowflake pipelines
recent_posts.summary: A team at Medium worked to reduce Snowflake costs by optimizing 22 expensive pipelines, implementing 56 changes. They focused on pragmatic solutions like eliminating unused services, reducing unnecessary data columns, adjusting pipeline schedules, improving query efficiency through explicit filtering and simpler predicates, and using time windows to avoid exponential data growth. They also modularized code for reuse and adjusted warehouse sizes for cost efficiency. Future plans include monitoring cost-efficiency tools and experimenting with advanced Snowflake features like Snowpipe Streaming.

recent_posts.title: Fixing subtle database errors that halted partner payments
recent_posts.summary: On September 5, 2024, a new Partner Program payments system was turned on, leading to an incident where 4,091 writers were wrongly informed they wouldn't be paid due to a subtle database race condition. The problem stemmed from the interaction between write and read operations on the database, exacerbated by the use of read replicas. The issue was mitigated by adjusting the sequence of database operations. Lessons were learned about managing race conditions and the necessity of simulating production environments during testing.

recent_posts.title: A New Era of Medium Engineering
recent_posts.summary: Medium's engineering team is embarking on a new era focused on long-term stability and success. Previous efforts were geared towards rapid improvement, but now the emphasis is on sustaining excellence and building a robust future. Key principles include prioritizing correctness, owning the 'how' in projects, adhering to processes, maintaining focus, and innovating uniquely. This transition aims to foster a world-class engineering culture that supports Medium's growth into a dependable multi-billion dollar company.

recent_posts.title: How to delete old data from DynamoDB without spending thousands
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses how to manage and reduce storage costs in DynamoDB by migrating necessary data to a new table and deleting outdated data. Three approaches are explored: doing nothing, deleting bad items directly, and migrating good items to a new table. Each method's costs and benefits are evaluated, emphasizing the importance of setting expiration dates for new data and accurately estimating costs prior to starting cleanup work.

recent_posts.title: How to do pagination in SwiftUI
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to do pagination in SwiftUI by using a generic container view, handling different states, and implementing lazy loading. The technique involves using a progress indicator, executing a task to load the next page, and making sure the task continues even if the view is not on screen.

recent_posts.title: Building a ChatGPT Plugin for Medium
recent_posts.summary: ChatGPT was trained on a dataset from 2021 and does not have direct access to the internet. ChatGPT can trigger the correct API of your plugins to retrieve a piece of content and do some manipulation on it. The Medium service is a simple middleware that convert hardcoded GraphQL queries and expose them in a REST API as JSON results.
